This August, I'm trading my usual commute for Iceland's gravel backcountry — 4 days, roughly 40-55 miles a day — to raise money for multiple myeloma research. I lead a team of scientists at Pfizer working to bring new medicines to multiple myeloma patients, including those in the earliest, pre-cancerous stages of the disease. I've spent my career in oncology drug discovery, and I know firsthand how long the road is from a promising molecule to a patient's bedside. That gap is exactly what I'm riding to help close. I'm joining the International Myeloma Foundation's Iceland Cycling Expedition, riding alongside myeloma patients themselves to fund research, education, and patient support. Some of what this ride funds: 🔬 The Black Swan Research Initiative — IMF's global effort to develop the first true cure for myeloma, funding 50+ research projects and clinical trials around one core strategy: detect the disease early and treat it aggressively, before it progresses. 🇮🇸 iStopMM — a Black Swan project screening over 80,000 adults in Iceland, the largest study of its kind for any cancer, testing whether early detection of myeloma precursors can save lives the same way mammograms and colonoscopies do for other cancers. As someone who works in this field, I don't take for granted how rare it is to get to put real dollars behind research I understand and believe in. I'll be sharing my training progress here weekly as I count down to Iceland — including this Sunday, riding alongside one of the patient participants I'll be pedaling next to on the trip. If you'd like to support this work, I'd be grateful for a donation to one of the patient riders, a share, or simply following along. 👉 https://lnkd.in/g_UaN-C7 #MyelomaIceland , #myeloma #multiplemyeloma , #myeloaresearch , #MMSM

FMI senior group leader Jeff Chao and his group have been awarded €2.5 million through the prestigious European Research Council (ERC) Advanced Grant scheme to study how RNA controls gene expression in living cells, with the goal of uncovering fundamental principles of RNA biology. The work could help understand how errors in these processes may contribute to neurodegeneration and muscle disease. Congratulations to Jeff and the whole team! https://lnkd.in/eG-zREg9

Accept. Smile. Laugh. Repeat. Laugh with the people you love. Laugh with those who challenge you. Laugh at life’s surprises. The day you stop letting bitterness define your story, life becomes lighter—and infinitely more beautiful. I truly believe that’s one of the greatest forms of success.

Three years ago today, I walked into GSK HQ for my first day and took this photo. I was excited, nervous, and had no idea what the next few years would bring. What I’ve learned since is that the people around you make all the difference. The work has been rewarding, but it’s the team I’m most grateful for. We’ve built something really special. A culture where we support and challenge each other, and still find plenty of moments to laugh along the way. That’s not something I take for granted. And the last few weeks have been a perfect reminder of why. In just three weeks, this incredible team has delivered four congresses and two major conferences. It’s been intense, at times challenging, but the collaboration, commitment, and energy behind it all has been pretty special to witness. Three years in, I still feel lucky to be part of this team. Here’s to everything we’ve learned, everything we’ve overcome, and everything still to come🧡 Joy Kelso Hannah De Bois Issy Broadhead Hannah Jackson Lucy Concannon Maria Clara Giuberti Tamagno Jessica (Nabitovsky) Levich Carmen Von Arnoldi
